findings.title: You're Back In The Room (Citrix NetScaler Pre-Auth RCE CVE-2026-8452(?))
findings.summary_md: Sina Kheirkhah at watchTowr Labs published a full pre-auth exploitation writeup on 14 Aug 2026, thirteen days before this story's first sighting. The research demonstrates unauthenticated remote code execution as root via a heap overflow in NetScaler's SAML ds:SignedInfo canonicalization, where an oversized InclusiveNamespaces PrefixList is copied into a fixed-size buffer in the nsppe packet engine, yielding a write-what-where primitive, RIP control by overwriting tx_pkt_complete_fptr, and a PHP webshell dropped at /var/vpn/theme/x.php on 13.1 before 13.1-63.18. The author notes Citrix did not confirm the CVE mapping but believes the bug is CVE-2026-8452 based on its memory-overflow description, and credits bulletin CTX696604 with the fix.

findings.title: Citrix Bulletin CTX696604: NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway Security Bulletin for CVE-2026-8451, CVE-2026-8452, CVE-2026-8655, CVE-2026-10816, CVE-2026-10817 and CVE-2026-13474
findings.summary_md: The Citrix bulletin that patched CVE-2026-8452 bundled fixes for six NetScaler CVEs in total, delivered in builds 14.1-72.61 and 13.1-63.18 (FIPS/NDcPP line 13.1-37.272). At publication Citrix described CVE-2026-8452 as a memory overflow leading to unpredictable behavior or denial of service and stated it had not observed any unmitigated exploitation. The Citrix support portal blocks direct crawling; the earliest Wayback Machine capture of the article is 2026-07-01T01:06:17Z, and reporting cited in this story places the advisory in June 2026.
